proposed_comments.title: Preserve cleared optional values in property-change notifications

confidence.rationale: The TS runtime serializes changed properties through JSON.stringify; an extension-visible optional property set to undefined is omitted from the outgoing payload, so the host never observes the clear and can retain the previous value.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve cleared optional values in property-change notifications

**Severity:** `high`

When an extension clears an optional observable property by setting it to `undefined`, the current `command/propChanged` serialization omits that property entirely. The C# adapters only update properties that arrive in the payload, so the host can keep stale title, subtitle, icon, or nested command state after the extension tried to clear it. Please normalize `undefined` changed-property values to JSON `null` before sending the notification and add a regression test that verifies the clear is present on the wire.

proposed_comments.title: Route property changes to the intended adapter target

confidence.rationale: The registry dispatches every property update to every registered target with the same command id. A command item and its nested command can share that id while exposing different properties, so item updates can mutate command state or vice versa.

proposed_comments.body:
### Route property changes to the intended adapter target

**Severity:** `high`

`command/propChanged` currently identifies only the command id. When a command item, fallback command item, list item, and the nested command use the same id, the C# registry fans the same payload out to all registered targets. That lets an item-level icon/title update overwrite the nested command cache, and it makes the resulting host state depend on registration order. Please add a small target-kind discriminator to the SDK/runtime notifications and filter dispatch on the C# side while preserving legacy fan-out when older extensions do not send the discriminator.

proposed_comments.title: Serialize status show/hide operations through provider disposal

confidence.rationale: ShowStatus and HideStatus are WinRT async actions, but the proxy starts hide/dispose work without waiting for a pending show to finish. An async host can therefore complete show after hide or provider disposal.

proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize status show/hide operations through provider disposal

**Severity:** `medium`

The status host methods return async actions, but the provider proxy can issue `HideStatus` or dispose while a prior `ShowStatus` is still incomplete. With an async host implementation, a pending show can finish after the hide path, leaving visible stale status UI for a disposed provider. Please queue status show/hide work so completion order matches request order, and make disposal wait for queued hides after any pending show. While touching this path, also preserve startup-notification ordering by draining the pre-initialization buffer before allowing new notifications to run inline.
